intro.ja:
玉は周囲八方向に一マス、飛車は縦横、角は斜めに何マスでも進みます。金は前方三マスと左右と真後ろ、銀は前方三マスと斜め後ろ二マスに一マス動きます。歩は一マス前、香は何マスでも前へ、桂は二マス前と一マス横を組み合わせて跳びます。前の向きは駒の所有者によって反対です。

飛車・角・香は途中の駒を飛び越せず、味方の駒があるマスには進めません。桂だけは途中の駒を飛び越します。龍は飛車の動きに斜め一マス、馬は角の動きに縦横一マスが加わります。成った歩・香・桂・銀は金の動きです。金の斜め後ろと銀の横・真後ろが動けない点を区別しましょう。
intro.en:
The king moves one square in any direction; rook and bishop slide along orthogonal and diagonal lines. A gold moves one square forward, sideways, backward, or diagonally forward. A silver moves straight forward or along any one-square diagonal. Pawns advance one square; lances slide forward; knights jump two squares forward and one sideways. Forward is relative to the piece’s owner.

Sliding pieces stop at blockers; friendly pieces cannot be captured. Only knights jump over intervening pieces. A dragon adds one-square diagonals to rook movement; a horse adds one-square orthogonal moves to bishop movement. Promoted pawn, lance, knight, and silver move as golds. Distinguish the gold’s missing backward diagonals from the silver’s missing sideways and straight-backward moves.

question.ja: 銀を真横へ一マス動かせますか？成銀ならどうですか？
question.en: Can a silver move one square sideways? What about a promoted silver?

answer.ja: 銀は動けません。成銀は金と同じなので真横へ動けます。
answer.en: An unpromoted silver cannot. A promoted silver moves as a gold and can.

courses.title: 駒の動き: 将棋の駒
courses.goalFormation:
将棋の駒
将棋の駒は表と裏にそれぞれ文字が書かれていて、表向きを「生駒」、裏向きを「成駒」と呼びます。
駒には表と裏がある
駒は基本的に盤上の四角いマスの中に置きます。囲碁は線の交点に石を置くので、そこが異なる点に注意しましょう。
駒はマス目に置く
王将と玉将は名前が違っても性能は同じで、裏は無地のため成駒はありません。王将は縦横斜めの全方向に1マスずつ動けます。飛車は前後左右にどこまでも動け、成駒の龍は飛車の動きに加えて斜めに1マス動けます。角は斜めにどこまでも動け、成駒の馬は角の動きに加えて前後左右に1マス動けます。飛車と角は成駒の動きも含めてセットで覚えるとよいでしょう。
王将(玉将)の動き
王将（玉将）は縦・横・ナナメのどのマスにも1マスずつ動けます。裏は無地で、成ることはありません。
飛車の動き
飛車は前後左右にどこまでも動けます。成ると龍になり、飛車の動きに加えてナナメにも1マス動けます。
角行の動き
角はナナメにどこまでも動けます。成ると馬になり、角の動きに加えて前後左右にも1マス動けます。
金将の動き
金は前後左右に1マスと、ナナメ前に1マス動けます。成ることはありません。
銀将の動き
銀はナナメの4方向と前に1マスずつ動けます。成銀は金と同じ動きになります。
桂馬の動き
桂馬は前に2マス・横に1マス進んだマスにだけ動け、後ろには下がれません。成桂は金と同じ動きです。
香車の動き
香車は前にどこまでも進めますが、前にしか動けません。成香は金と同じ動きです。
歩兵の動き
歩は前に1マスだけ動けます。成ると「と金」になり、金と同じ動きになります。
自陣と敵陣
敵陣まで進めた駒は成ってパワーアップできます。飛車・角・香車は遠くまで動けますが、途中に他の駒があると飛び越せません。例外は桂馬だけで、他の駒を飛び越せます。
駒を飛び越すことはできない
相手の駒があるマスに動かすとその駒を取れます。取った駒は駒台に置いておき、好きなときに使えます。
相手の駒を取れる
金と銀は動きが似ているため、初心者が最も混乱しやすい駒です。違いを複数の視点で比べて覚え方を紹介します。
金将と銀将の動きの違い（青丸が動ける方向）
金は前・斜め前・横・真後ろの6方向に動け、成れません。銀は前・斜め前・斜め後ろの5方向に動け、成ると金と同じ動き(成銀)になります。最大の違いは、金は横と真後ろに動ける代わりに斜め後ろへ動けず、銀は斜め後ろに動ける代わりに横と真後ろへ動けない点です。形では金は「十字+斜め前」、銀は「前方3マス+斜め後ろ」でイチョウの葉のような形です。役割も異なり、金は横を固められるので守り(囲いの一部として玉の近く)、銀は攻めた後に斜め後ろへ退却できるので攻め(棒銀など)に向きます。横に動きたければ金、斜め後ろへ引きたければ銀、前進はどちらでも可能です。銀は成れば金と同じ動きになるため、攻めに使った後は守りにも使えます。

root.commentEn:
Shogi pieces
Each shogi piece has characters on both sides: the front side is the unpromoted piece (生駒) and the back side is the promoted piece (成駒).
Each piece has a front and a back
Pieces are placed inside the square cells of the board. Unlike Go, where stones go on line intersections, shogi pieces sit within squares, so take care.
Pieces are placed on the squares
The king (王将) and jade general (玉将) differ in name but move identically, and have a blank reverse so they cannot promote. The king moves one square in any of the eight directions. The rook moves any distance forward, back, left or right, and its promoted form, the dragon, adds one-square diagonal moves. The bishop moves any distance diagonally, and its promoted form, the horse, adds one-square orthogonal moves. It is best to learn rook and bishop together with their promoted forms.
King movement
The king moves one square in any direction: forward, backward, sideways or diagonally. Its back is blank, so it never promotes.
Rook movement
The rook moves any distance forward, backward or sideways. Promoted, it becomes a dragon and can also move one square diagonally.
Bishop movement
The bishop moves any distance diagonally. Promoted, it becomes a horse and can also move one square forward, backward or sideways.
Gold movement
The gold moves one square forward, backward or sideways, and one square diagonally forward. It does not promote.
Silver movement
The silver moves one square diagonally in any of four directions or one square straight forward. A promoted silver moves like a gold.
Knight movement
The knight moves only to a square two ahead and one to the side, and can never move backward. A promoted knight moves like a gold.
Lance movement
The lance moves any distance straight forward and nowhere else. A promoted lance moves like a gold.
Pawn movement
The pawn moves one square forward. Promoted, it becomes a tokin and moves like a gold.
Your camp and the enemy camp
A piece that reaches the enemy camp can promote and become stronger. The rook, bishop and lance move long distances but cannot jump over pieces in their path; the knight is the sole exception and can jump over other pieces.
Pieces cannot jump over other pieces
Moving onto a square holding an opponent's piece captures it. Captured pieces are kept on the komadai and can be used whenever you like.
Capturing the opponent's pieces
Gold and silver have similar movement and are the pieces beginners confuse most. Below they are compared from several angles to help you remember them.
Difference between gold and silver movement (blue circles show where it can move)
The gold moves in six directions (forward, diagonally forward, sideways, straight back) and cannot promote; the silver moves in five (forward, diagonally forward, diagonally back) and promotes to a piece that moves like gold. The key difference: gold can go sideways and straight back but not diagonally back, while silver can retreat diagonally but not sideways or straight back. Gold is shaped like a cross plus diagonal-forward squares; silver is three forward squares plus the back diagonals, like a ginkgo leaf. Their roles differ: gold guards the king's sides and fits defence (castles), while silver can retreat after attacking and suits offence such as Bogin (Climbing Silver). If you need to move sideways it is gold, if you need to retreat diagonally it is silver, and both can advance. A silver promoted after attacking moves like gold, so it can also serve in defence.
